title: The Gospel and Atonement
explanation: The Gospel is the good news that Jesus Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, was buried, and rose again the third day. His death was substitutionary — He bore the penalty sinners deserved.
logical_reasoning: God is just and must punish sin. Yet God is love and desires to save. The cross satisfies both justice and mercy: sin is punished in Christ, and sinners are forgiven through faith.
defense_response: The atonement is not symbolic. Scripture teaches substitution (Isaiah 53:5), propitiation (Romans 3:25), and imputation (2 Corinthians 5:21).

title: Salvation by Grace Through Faith
explanation: Salvation is a gift of God received by grace through faith, not by works. Repentance and belief in Christ bring justification before God.
logical_reasoning: If salvation were by works, grace would not be grace. A perfect God requires perfect righteousness, which only Christ provides.
defense_response: James 2 discusses evidence of faith, not earning salvation. Works demonstrate genuine faith but do not produce salvation.

title: Biblical Doctrine of the Trinity
explanation: There is one God in three distinct Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Each is fully God, yet there is one divine essence.
logical_reasoning: Scripture affirms monotheism (Deut 6:4), affirms the deity of Christ (John 1:1), affirms the deity of the Spirit (Acts 5:3-4), and yet distinguishes persons (Matthew 28:19).
defense_response: The Trinity is not three gods. It is one being with three persons. Modalism and Arianism contradict Scripture.

title: Deity and Humanity of Christ
explanation: Jesus Christ is fully God and fully man. He took on human flesh while remaining divine.
logical_reasoning: Only God can save, and only man can represent humanity. Therefore Christ must be both divine and human.
defense_response: Jesus forgave sins, accepted worship, and existed before Abraham (John 8:58), proving divine identity.

title: Sin and Human Nature
explanation: All humanity is fallen in Adam. Sin affects the heart and separates man from God.
logical_reasoning: Universal moral failure proves universal corruption. A holy God cannot overlook sin without justice.
defense_response: Human goodness does not erase guilt. Scripture declares all have sinned and need redemption.

title: Messianic Prophecy Fulfillment
explanation: Old Testament prophecy predicted the Messiah's birth, death, and mission. Jesus fulfills these prophecies precisely.
logical_reasoning: Prophecies written centuries before Christ align with His life, demonstrating divine authorship of Scripture.
defense_response: The specificity of birthplace (Micah 5:2) and crucifixion imagery (Psalm 22) cannot be coincidence.

title: Historical Resurrection of Christ
explanation: Jesus physically rose from the dead and appeared to many witnesses.
logical_reasoning: The empty tomb, eyewitness testimony, and transformation of the apostles support the historical resurrection.
defense_response: Hallucination theories fail because multiple group appearances occurred.

title: Authority and Inspiration of Scripture
explanation: All Scripture is inspired by God and is truth.
logical_reasoning: A truthful God communicates truthfully. Scripture's unity across centuries confirms divine inspiration.
defense_response: Apparent contradictions resolve through context and careful interpretation.

title: Second Coming and Final Judgment
explanation: Christ will return bodily. There will be resurrection, judgment, and a new heaven and earth.
logical_reasoning: Justice demands final accountability. God's promises guarantee restoration.
defense_response: Symbolic interpretations cannot cancel clear teaching of bodily return.
